tagline: A stone turnpike close enough to the falls to hear them.
intro: Georgetown Pike leaves Leesburg Pike at Dranesville and runs east 11.79 miles to Langley. It passes the village center of Great Falls, follows the edge of Great Falls Park, then drops through sharp curves into the valley of Difficult Run.

The road went down between 1813 and 1827 as a crowned stone highway, laid in large stone a foot deep at the center by the turnpike company's own account. The Potomac is never in sight from it, but at Great Falls the pike passes close enough to hear the water. In 1974 it became the first Virginia Byway.

moments.title: Great Falls
moments.text: The village went by Forestville, unofficially, since another Forestville already had the post office, until 1955, when it took the name of the falls nearby.

moments.title: Difficult Run
moments.text: Long-boatmen of the Patowmack Company named the stream for the treacherous bends of the Potomac near its mouth, and the pike takes a run of sharp curves down into its valley.

moments.title: Bull Neck Run
moments.text: Past the Madeira School the pike crosses Bull Neck Run, where an original road bridge with a stone and brick viaduct survives from the turnpike builders.
